summary: IGNIS (Intelligent Guidance for Next-generation In-Space Safety) is an interactive, source-grounded research intelligence platform built to make decades of archived NASA microgravity combustion science accessible, comparable, and actionable. Developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Flame in Freefall),the platform ingests 8 verified flight investigations from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository—spanning 176+ experimental observations, 12 calibrated imagery records, and official NTRS technical documentation across droplet combustion, solid fabric flammability, and gaseous jet liftoff. In microgravity, the absence of buoyant convection causes flames to burn cooler, assume spherical structures, and produce low-temperature "cool flames" that evade conventional spacecraft sensors. IGNIS addresses this challenge through three core scientific innovations: an auditable comparability engine that enforces dimensional homogeneity and blocks invalid cross-regime data overlays,an evidence gap heatmap that identifies uncharacterized environmental conditions,and a 100%offline, citation-grounded research assistant that ties every finding directly to NASA DOIs.As long-duration crewed exploration advances toward the Moon and Mars under the Artemis program,understanding orbital flammability boundaries is mission-critical. IGNIS empowers aerospace engineers and researchers to query,compare,and verify microgravity combustion data with uncompromising scientific integrity.
details:
IGNIS (Intelligent Guidance for Next-generation In-Space Safety) is an interactive, source-grounded research intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Flame in Freefall). The platform ingests, unifies, and analyzes archived microgravity combustion flight data across 8 verified NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations—including FLEX (PSI-69) and FLEX-2 (PSI-70) droplet combustion aboard the ISS, SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98) and SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99) large-scale solid fabric flame spread aboard Cygnus, BASS (PSI-108) polymer regression, and SPICE (PSI-107), SLICE (PSI-71), and ACME-BRE (PSI-101) gaseous jet liftoff and burning flux emulations. Through an interactive Showdown-style command center, researchers can inspect 176+ verified observations, plot time-series telemetry (d2d^2d2 droplet decay, flame spread progression, and smoke point liftoff), evaluate cross-experiment comparability, map unexplored environmental parameters, and query technical literature with an offline assistant that cites official NASA DOIs.

The primary benefit of IGNIS is that it transforms fragmented spreadsheets, camera archives, and technical reports into a scientifically rigorous, unified workspace. Crucially, it incorporates an automated comparability engine that enforces dimensional homogeneity and physical regime integrity, actively preventing researchers from making invalid cross-regime overlays (such as liquid droplet regression versus solid fabric pyrolysis). Furthermore, the multi-factor evidence gap heatmap plots tested versus uncharacterized spacecraft cabin conditions (Oxygen % vs. Pressure vs. Forced Airflow), pinpointing untested fire hazards before mission deployment.

As human spaceflight advances toward the Moon and Mars under the Artemis program, understanding combustion in reduced gravity is mission-critical. In microgravity, the absence of buoyancy causes flames to burn cooler, assume spherical structures, and generate invisible "cool flames" that evade conventional spacecraft smoke detectors. IGNIS bridges raw spaceflight telemetry and future habitat fire safety protocols, giving engineers, material scientists, and mission planners reliable tools to assess material flammability and design resilient detection systems.

The platform was built from the ground up using a modern, reliable stack: Python 3.11 and FastAPI for the asynchronous REST backend, SQLite3 for normalized relational data storage with verified SHA-256 source manifests, and React 19 with TypeScript, Vite, Recharts, and Lucide React for the responsive frontend interface. Quality and reliability were verified through an automated test suite with 29/29 passing backend tests and clean TypeScript compilation.

IGNIS is uniquely creative in its synthesis of aerospace mission control aesthetics with strict physics guardrails. Rather than deploying an opaque, hallucination-prone generative chatbot, the platform uses a 100% deterministic, offline citation retrieval model that runs locally without external API keys or cloud dependencies. Every observation, measurement unit, and literature citation is grounded strictly in authentic NASA datasets, delivering an accessible, resilient, and scientifically honest tool dedicated to orbital fire safety.
